html:
In April 2006 mass protests in Nepal, the second People's Movement, forced King Gyanendra to give up the full power he had seized. In May 2008 an elected assembly abolished the monarchy and made Nepal a republic.

The protests were led by the main parties, allied with the Maoist rebels of the civil war. After nineteen days of strikes and curfews the king restored parliament. A peace deal in November 2006 ended the war and brought the Maoists into politics; they won the most seats in the 2008 election.

On 28 May 2008 the assembly ended the line of kings begun by Prithvi Narayan Shah in the 1760s. Writing a constitution took until 2015, when a federal constitution created seven provinces. Discontent with the parties that came to power led to the Gen Z protests of 2025.
sum: In April 2006 mass protests in Nepal, the second People's Movement, forced King Gyanendra to give up the full power he had seized. In May 2008 an elected assembly abolished the monarchy and made Nepal a republic.
